CHIEF COMPLAINT
Routine yearly exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Christine is a 63-year-old female presenting for her routine annual physical examination. She reports that her depression has been well-controlled with her current medication and weekly therapy sessions. She is sleeping well, getting a full eight hours per night, and denies any suicidal ideation. Regarding her hypertension, she reports that her blood pressure readings have been variable over the past couple of weeks, fluctuating between high and low readings without stabilizing. She is compliant with her blood pressure medication. She attributes some recent headaches to prolonged computer screen exposure at work. She reports that her diet has been inconsistent due to work stress and increased work hours, leading to reliance on frozen meals and limited time for grocery shopping and meal preparation. She denies numbness or tingling in her hands or fingers. Her right wrist carpal tunnel release surgery from approximately two years ago continues to do well.

Positive for occasional headaches attributed to computer screen use. Negative for numbness or tingling in hands or fingers. Negative for chest pain, shortness of breath, or other systemic symptoms.
